claim: The only automated check that no ERPNext call uses a side door is the fake's `_door` detector, which the integration fixture runs on every call. No test shows the detector actually flags a door, so a broken detector would let the whole suite pass. Also, no test checks across all tools that no input schema has a DocType, report, method, field-list, filter or path property; only list_items is tried with `doctype` and `fields`.
evidence: tests/integration/conftest.py:25 asserts `fake.doors == []`. `_door`, DOOR_METHODS and METHOD_ROUTE are in tests/fakes/erpnext.py:1008-1060. Grep finds no test outside the fake that refers to `_door`, `doors` or DOOR_METHODS. tests/e2e/test_ceiling.py tests ERPNext's limits on the agent's key, not the calls Enterich makes. The schema-property check is only test_master_data.py::test_inputs_outside_the_schema_are_refused_before_erpnext (list_items, `doctype`/`fields`).
proposal: Add a unit test that feeds `_door` one request per door and asserts it names each one: DELETE, a body with docstatus 1, `amended_from`, a nested `doc` string with docstatus 2, the `run_method` parameter, every DOOR_METHODS entry on v1, v2 and v2-document method routes, and savedocs with action Submit. In the same test, assert it returns None for a resource path or parameter value such as `X?run_method=discard`. Also add a test that walks every tool's inputSchema and fails on any property named or titled doctype, report, method, fields, filters or path.

verdict.reason: Confirmed with a mutant. In a scratch copy of the repo, I made `_door` (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:1036) return None straight away. `uv run pytest tests/unit tests/integration` still passed: 820 tests, plus the snapshot. So the side-door detector named as evidence in the Definition of Done of REQ-001-PRS-F006 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:277-279: "FakeErpnext refuses and records every such call, and each integration test fails on one") is never shown to flag anything. tests/integration/conftest.py:25 (`fake.doors == []`) passes trivially when the detector is broken. Outside the fake, tests/ never mentions `_door`, `DOOR_METHODS` or `METHOD_ROUTE`. The tests that use names like `X?run_method=discard` (test_master_data.py:203, test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:911) only check the other direction, that the detector doesn't flag a name in a path. The docstatus cases in test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:248-250 are input-schema refusals and never reach the fake. tests/e2e/test_ceiling.py checks the agent key's rights in ERPNext, not the calls Enterich makes. A unit test of `_door` that feeds it each kind of door and also the false-positive cases closes the gap within the current specs. The schema half of the finding is weaker. tests/integration/test_tool_list.py snapshots every inputSchema for review, which is the "inspection" route the DoD allows. No property in the snapshot today is named doctype, report, method, fields, filters or path. Still, a walk over all tools that fails on those names is a cheap regression guard and fits in the same fix.

claim: For purchase invoices, only the create without a template is tested. No test shows that a purchase create with a template given, an update clearing the template, an update of only the remarks, or an update giving a template behaves as the sales side does.
evidence: test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py::test_a_purchase_draft_warns_of_item_tax_rows is the only purchase test that sets `erp.item_taxes`. The purchase update path calls drafts.tax_warning at src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py:394, but no test with item tax rows covers it. The sales cases are test_a_given_template_takes_the_place_of_item_tax_rows, test_clearing_the_template_warns_of_item_tax_rows and test_item_tax_rows_warn_again_until_a_template_replaces_them.
proposal: Parametrise, or copy for purchase invoices, the three sales tests named above: with `erp.item_taxes['PAPER']` set, a create giving a purchase template has no warning; an update with `taxes_and_charges=''` and an update of only `remarks` return the item-tax warning; an update giving a template returns none.

verdict.reason: The gap is real. Item 3 of REQ-001-PRS-F020's Definition of Done (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:478) says "A purchase invoice draft does the same". That includes the update cases in item 2 at line 477: clearing the template warns, an update of only the remarks warns, and an update giving a template doesn't. In the integration tests, the only purchase test that sets `erp.item_taxes` is tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py:200, test_a_purchase_draft_warns_of_item_tax_rows. It covers only a create without a template, and the singular wording. The sales tests for these cases are at tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:429-455 and have no purchase counterpart. In tests/e2e, test_drafts.py:199 (reverse charge) covers only a purchase create with a template given. It asserts warnings == [] on an item that has an item tax template. The only e2e purchase-update test is test_drafts.py:396 (bill_no), and test_tax_rules.py:67 covers only a create. So no test covers a purchase update together with item tax rows. Mutant check: I copied the repo into the scratchpad and replaced the purchase update's `warnings += drafts.tax_warning(saved, inputs.taxes_and_charges)` with `pass` (src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py:394). The unit and integration suites still passed in full, 820 tests. So nothing observes the purchase update's tax warnings. Copying or parametrising the three sales tests for purchase invoices, with `erp.item_taxes['PAPER']` set, closes the gap within the current specs. No change to the specs or ADRs is needed.

claim: No test covers a page that returns exactly `limit` records with none beyond, so `has_more` being true at len(records) == limit goes unnoticed.
evidence: enterich.shapes.x_page__mutmut_9 (len(records) >= limit). The existing has_more tests (test_master_data.py:44, :72, :75, test_procure_to_pay.py:343, test_record_to_report.py:330) fetch either fewer than limit or limit+1 records.
proposal: Unit test: page([{...}, {...}], offset=0, limit=2)["has_more"] is False, and with three records it is True. Or an integration list with exactly `limit` matching records asserts has_more False.

verdict.reason: The finding holds. `page` (src/enterich/shapes.py:191-201) sets `has_more` to `len(records) > limit` and is given `limit + 1` fetched records (docstring at :192; master_data.py:58 and the other callers listed by grep). `mutmut show enterich.shapes.x_page__mutmut_9` reports the mutant as survived, with the diff `len(records) >= limit`. The mutant is not equivalent: when exactly `limit` records match, the mutant says `has_more` is True, and the tool descriptions in tests/snapshots/tools.json promise that "`has_more` says whether `offset` can fetch more". REQ-001-PRS-F014 and the list shape (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:385, :581, and :207) require `has_more`, so the behaviour is required and visible to the caller. I searched every `has_more` assertion in tests/, including tests/e2e. None of them sees exactly `limit` records: - tests/unit/test_shapes.py:182 passes 1 record with limit 10. - test_master_data.py:44 gets 3 items with the default limit 20. - test_master_data.py:72/75, test_order_to_cash.py:511/515, test_procure_to_pay.py:343 and test_record_to_report.py:330 fetch either limit+1 or fewer. - test_order_to_cash.py:469 has 1 row. - e2e test_record_to_report.py:106/125 fetch pages of 100 from a chart of accounts whose size is not fixed. My throwaway test in the scratchpad (page of 2 records with limit 2 gives has_more False; 3 records with limit 2 gives True) passes on the current code. On the mutant its first assert must fail, since 2 >= 2. The gap closes with that unit test in tests/unit/test_shapes.py, within the current specs; no code change is needed.

claim: The DoD item on durations (a 1 s delayed fake, 3 calls, ERPNext duration of at least 3 s within the total) has no test. The only assertion is `duration >= erpnext_duration >= 0`, so integer rounding, a constant 3 or a total of monotonic()+started all pass.
evidence: enterich.tools.x__log__mutmut_45, _46, _47, _48 (duration: round(..., None), round(3), round(...) without places, monotonic() + started), _51, _53 (erpnext_duration rounded to an integer). The only check is tests/integration/test_master_data.py:330.
proposal: Integration test: erp.delay = 0.25 on a create making three ERPNext calls. Assert erpnext_calls == 3, 0.75 <= erpnext_duration <= duration, and duration < 0.75 + 2 (an upper bound). The fractional delay kills the integer-rounding mutants, since the values would come out 0 or 1.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds. The second Definition of Done item of REQ-002-PRS-NF008 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:223) asks for a test where a fake ERPNext delays each answer by 1 s, a create makes three ERPNext calls, and the log shows 3 calls and an ERPNext duration of at least 3 s within the total duration. No such test exists.

I searched all of tests/, including tests/e2e. The only checks on the log's duration fields are tests/integration/test_master_data.py:329-330 (`erpnext_calls == 1` and `duration >= erpnext_duration >= 0`, on a fast list_items).

Uses of `erp.delay` at test_master_data.py:342 and :352 only test timeouts, not log fields. tests/unit/test_erpnext.py:311-315 checks `Meter.seconds >= 0.1` directly, which never reaches the rounding in `_log` (src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:363-365).

`mutmut show` confirms the mutants as described:
- `_45`: `round(..., None)`
- `_46`: `round(3)`
- `_47`: `round(...)` without places
- `_48`: `monotonic() + started`
- `_51` and `_53`: `round(meter.seconds, None)` and `round(meter.seconds)`

None of them is equivalent, and all pass the current test. On a fast fake, 0 >= 0 >= 0 holds, a constant 3 is at least the near-zero ERPNext duration, and `monotonic() + started` is large.

The proposed test closes the gap within the current specs. With a 0.25 s delay on a three-call create:
- Asserting `erpnext_calls == 3` and `0.75 <= erpnext_duration <= duration` kills the integer-rounding mutants, since they give 0 or 1.
- An upper bound on `duration` kills `round(3)` and `monotonic() + started`.

A literal 1 s version of the Definition of Done item would not kill `_51` or `_53` (3.0x rounds to 3), so the fractional delay, or a check that the value is not a whole number, is needed. It needs no spec or ADR change.

claim: No test checks that a get returns yes/no fields as JSON booleans, so dropping `flags` (is_return returned as 0/1) passes, because the dict-equality asserts treat 0 == False.
evidence: enterich.tools.x_get_document__mutmut_25 (flags=flags removed). The only get_document caller that passes flags is invoicing.get_invoice (flags={"is_return"}). tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay.py:213 compares the whole result with "is_return": False by ==, which 0 satisfies. The list test in test_order_to_cash.py:253 uses `is False`, but only for the list. The DoD item "yes/no fields are booleans" is not met for gets.
proposal: In the get_sales_invoice / get_purchase_invoice integration tests, assert `result["is_return"] is False` (and `is True` for a return invoice whose fake has is_return=1), or compare the raw result text for `"is_return": false`.

verdict.reason: I couldn't refute this finding. `mutmut show enterich.tools.x_get_document__mutmut_25` reports the mutant as survived. It drops `flags=flags` from `shape(...)` at src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:235, and the mutant is not equivalent: a get would return `is_return` as 0 or 1 instead of false or true. The only `get_document` caller that passes flags is the one at src/enterich/tools/invoicing.py:245 (`flags={"is_return"}`), used by get_sales_invoice and get_purchase_invoice. The behaviour is required: the conventions at docs/specs/req-001-core.md:585 return yes/no fields as true/false, and the REQ-001-PRS-F014 Definition of Done at req-001-core.md:385 says "yes/no fields are booleans". I searched all of tests/, tests/e2e included, and no test closes the gap. tests/integration/test_order_to_cash.py:278 and tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay.py:213 compare the whole get result by `==` with `"is_return": False`, which 0 also passes. The `is False` check at test_order_to_cash.py:253 covers only list_sales_invoices. The type-checked booleans at tests/integration/test_master_data.py:153-154 are for master data, which goes through a different path. tests/e2e/test_invoicing.py:73 and :169 never look at `is_return`. The asserts at tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:543/607 read the ERPNext document directly. The tools snapshot has no outputSchema that could catch the type. Closing it needs only a test within the current specs: in the get_sales_invoice and get_purchase_invoice integration tests, assert `result["is_return"] is False`, and optionally `is True` for a return invoice. Such a test would fail on the mutant, because `0 is False` is false.
